extracted.intended_audience: comics-industry professionals (creators, editors, publishers, distributors, retailers), prospective Eisner voters, nominees, and judges
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, eligibility, procedures, and category definitions for the Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards and Eisner Hall of Fame (voter eligibility, judge selection, Hall of Fame eligiblity, award categories, and relevant deadlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter eligibility (general Eisner Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Online voting will be available to professionals in the comics industry, including creators, editors, publishers, distributors, and retailers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those eligible include comic book/graphic novel/webcomic creators (writers, artists, cartoonists, pencillers, inkers, letterers, colorists); comic book/graphic novel publishers and editors; comics historians and educators; graphic novel librarians; and owners and managers of comic book specialty retail stores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter application requirement (new in 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: All prospective Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards voters must apply to be considered to vote before the nominees are announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new applications will be processed once nominees are announced. Voting applications will close on May 13, 2026. Those who were invited to vote for the 2026 Hall of Fame are already eligible and do not need to re-register. An email notifying currently registered voters was sent April 28, 2026; not receiving the email implies not registered and requires applying prior to the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step voting process for Eisner Hall of Fame
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-step voting process has been put in place for enhanced security for Hall of Fame voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: New prospective voters apply via a provided online form (link given). After filling out the form, eligible voters will be invited to go to the ballot and cast their votes. Individuals previously approved to vote will be sent an invitation and do not need to re-register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hall of Fame eligibility — significant contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the Hall of Fame, the person must have made a significant contribution to the comic book/graphic storytelling medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of significant contribution include creating a major character (or characters), producing memorable stories considered 'classics,' having an art style that influenced numerous others, innovating storytelling devices in the medium, advancing comics publishing, or otherwise having a lasting influence on the industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hall of Fame eligibility — 35-year first-professional-work rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The person’s first professional work must have occurred at least 35 years before the year of the awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the cited year, the page gives the cutoff example: first professional work must have occurred by 1991 for that year's awards (or 1990 for the other year referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting deadline (Hall of Fame)
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for voting is March 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This appears in the Hall of Fame voting section; applicants must complete the two-step process and cast votes by this deadline where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges selection (general Eisner Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges are chosen by Comic-Con’s awards subcommittee and are selected to represent all aspects of the comics industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcommittee is made up of individuals from the board of directors, staff, and various departments. Judges are selected to represent creators, retailers, graphic novel librarians, academics/historians, and journalists/reviewers. The judges will select the nominees that will be placed on the Eisner Awards ballot in some 30 categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate Hall of Fame judging panel
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate panel of judges selects the Eisner Hall of Fame inductees and nominees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Hall of Fame judging panel is distinct from the general awards judges; Hall of Fame judges nominate a group of nominees from which industry voters elect inductees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Works eligibility by publication year
rubrics_metrics.description: Eisner Awards for a given year reward excellence for works published in the prior year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example on the page: the 2025 Eisner Awards rewarded works published in 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will Eisner Spirit of Comics Retailer Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to a store that has done an outstanding job of supporting the comics art medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is measured both in the community and within the industry at large (example: past winner Akira Comics of Madrid, Spain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bob Clampett Humanitarian Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recognizing humanitarian work in the comic book industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: award presented to organizations or efforts (Mad Cave Studios won for the L.A. Strong charity comic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Russ Manning Promising Newcomer Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Award for a promising newcomer in comics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented to an artist judged to show promising talent; context: presentation and past presenters listed but detailed rubric not specified on page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill Finger Award for Excellence in Comic Book Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recognizing excellence in comic book writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented annually; page lists recipients and presenters but does not give a detailed scoring rubric beyond the award title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bob Clampett / other special awards — examples of domain-specific criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Special awards (humanitarian, retailer, newcomer, writing recognition) have domain-specific criteria tied to charitable impact, retail support, newcomer promise, or writing excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page gives examples of recipients and the rationale (charitable comic, retail community impact, promising newcomer, excellence in writing) but does not detail formal scoring rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges’ responsibilities — selecting nominees
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges read and select nominees which will be placed on the Eisner Awards ballot in some 30 categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once nominations are announced they will be voted on by professionals in the comics industry; separate Hall of Fame panel handles Hall of Fame nominations/inductees.
